questions.q: According to the lesson, why isn't a YAML file alone a strong portfolio piece?
options: Because YAML files cannot be stored in a public repository
Because it doesn't demonstrate the decision-making and understanding behind the choices made
Because interviewers never look at code
Because GitHub does not support YAML files
questions.explain: A YAML file alone proves you can copy a tutorial. What demonstrates real understanding is the reasoning behind the choices — captured in a README, decision note, and the ability to explain it.

questions.q: What four things does the lesson say should be included in the portfolio piece?
options: A resume, a cover letter, references, and a transcript
A clean public repository, a README explaining the why, screenshots of a real pipeline run, and a short decision note
Only the Dockerfile, nothing else
A video game demo unrelated to the pipeline
questions.explain: The portfolio piece should include the repo itself, a README explaining the reasoning behind choices, proof of a real execution (screenshots), and a short decision note on what was built and scoped out.

questions.q: When an interviewer asks 'why did production need approval but staging didn't?', what are they really testing?
options: Whether you memorized the YAML syntax
Whether you understand the difference between Continuous Delivery and Continuous Deployment
Whether you know how to spell 'approval'
Whether Kubernetes was used
questions.explain: This question tests whether the candidate understands Continuous Delivery (human-gated) vs. Continuous Deployment (fully automatic), not just whether they copied a working pattern.

questions.q: How does the capstone pipeline connect back to DORA metrics from Chapter 1?
options: It doesn't connect at all — DORA only applies to large companies
The pipeline is a concrete example you can point to for metrics like lead time (automatic staging deploys) and change failure rate (tests blocking bad merges)
DORA metrics can only be measured with expensive third-party software
The capstone replaces the need for any metrics
questions.explain: The capstone pipeline provides real, tangible evidence for DORA metrics — e.g., automatic staging deployment demonstrates short lead time, and a real test suite blocking bad merges demonstrates a lower change failure rate.

questions.q: What is the broader significance of this capstone within the DevOps Engineer path?
options: It is a completely standalone exercise with no connection to later courses
The patterns practiced here (build, test, gate, deploy) carry forward into later courses on configuration management and monitoring in the same path
It replaces the need to take any further courses
It is only relevant to companies using GitHub Actions
questions.explain: The lesson notes this capstone closes out CI/CD Pipelines specifically, but the same build/test/gate/deploy patterns continue to apply in later courses in the broader DevOps Engineer path.
